subject: Frequency bands as species/ species groups?

messages.author: 171a427b5e807550
messages.subject: Frequency bands as species/ species groups?
parts:
Hello all, 
I am new to acoustic ecology. I have been analyzing some of the large recordings (20hrs) I made during my field work in Mozambique. 
I intend to get some index of species using the frequency bands. 
If I understand it right, the frequency band + sound intensity / amplitude envelope in the soundscape can be considered equivalent to species in a landscape. 
I need some help in understanding what is the best way of getting all the unique frequency + amplitude peaks in a large recording. Should I split the big file in to smaller segments, or is there a way to define smaller bins in a large files. 

I used the mean spec function and find peaks. Is there any other way to do it? 
Also, what is a good way to filter out the wind + anthrophoneic noises that I am not interested in. Will be glad for help. 

regards
Hemant

messages.author: bfa183f4897a5619
messages.subject: Re: [seewave] Frequency bands as species/ species groups?
parts:
Hi Hemant,

A good place to get started might be the ACI function in seewave. However, you will need to study the literature on mapping acoustic complexity to species richness. It's not as simple as their being "equivalent"! Here is a paper on the subject: http://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1470160X10002037

best wishes,
jesse

messages.subject: Re: [seewave] Frequency bands as species/ species groups?
parts:
Hello, 
So from the ACI paper, I understand that ACI is basically an indicator of community in a temporal bin. What I am looking for is a method of unsupervised spectral classification after filtering out wind + anthopophony + other non bird calls/songs. Theoretically where each peak of frequency + amplitude represents a species. It may give out of lot of false positives but then I am ready to spend time in trying to reduce that as a next step. 

Can someone please guide me on this pinting out specific functions that I can use in seewave to do this. I have been playing with meanspec, spec and find peaks that sort of give me what I am looking for. but I am sure if I am doing a right thing. 

Will be super grateful. 

Thanks

messages.author: 4271370c9274971b
messages.subject: Re: [seewave] Frequency bands as species/ species groups?
parts:
Hemant,

If you're looking for a way to automatically quantify different species calls, a good start might be to look into the warbleR package. warbleR includes the function xcorr(), which correlates two spectrograms of interest. So you could create a template spectrogram for a given species call, then use xcorr to cross-correlate the template with segments (of length(template)) of your sample waveform. Setting a high correlation threshold (e.g. r = 0.75) would at least narrow down your data to a set of candidate sounds for further inspection. This will be computationally expensive.

There may be an analogous function in seewave but I'm not familiar with it. Hopefully that helps

Sean
